oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: High error rate and timeouts observed on model endpoint /v1/generate (region: eu-west-1). Error rate > 8% and tail latency > 10s for last 5m. Paging SRE oncall. Pager: @Sofia L :rotating_light:
Sofia L: on it, paging handoff in 5. Can someone pull recent deploys+variant traffic?
Raj P: I see a spike from keys mapped to beta-neon-v3. 70% of requests to that variant, stable-llama-v2 is healthy but low traffic.
Evelyn M: Confirmed. Rolling error rate coincides with canary traffic shift at 11:02 UTC. Logs show CUDA OOMs on a subset of hosts: oom_kill process: inference-runner.
Miguel C: Not seeing infra-wide OOMs, looks like narrow subset with quantized kernel fallback enabled. Suspect regression in beta-neon-v3 kernels.
Priya K: Customer impact: 3 customers report timeouts intermittently (enterprise keys). Opening quick support thread.
Sofia L: Decision: temporarily demote beta-neon-v3 -> reduce to 0% traffic, shift to stable-llama-v2 as fallback. Also apply per-key soft-throttle to heavy keys to reduce amplification. Anyone oppose?
Raj P: +1. Suggest using routing policy: weighted-fallback and enforce per-key QPS caps.
Evelyn M: I'll run the routing change. Command: ```redwoodctl routing set-weights --model beta-neon-v3=0 --model stable-llama-v2=1 --region eu-west-1```
Miguel C: Also applying emergency per-key throttles: ```redwoodctl quotas update --scope keys --expr "qps>20" --action throttle --limit 10``` This will be non-blocking but reduce spike.
Sofia L: Go ahead, do it. Also push a circuit-breaker on the variant as a safety net: ```redwoodctl variants deactivate beta-neon-v3 --reason "OOM regression" --force```
oncall-bot: USER ACTION: Routing weights updated by Evelyn M at 11:14 UTC. beta-neon-v3 -> 0%, stable-llama-v2 -> 100% for eu-west-1.
oncall-bot: USER ACTION: Variant beta-neon-v3 deactivated by Sofia L at 11:15 UTC.
PagerDuty: Pager acknowledged by Sofia L.
Raj P: Monitoring: error rate dropped to 1.2% in 2m after reroute. Tail latency back within SLOs.
Priya K: Notified affected customers with interim mitigation note, offering point of contact. One enterprise customer requested SLA credit info, opened support ticket #INC-8279.
Evelyn M: Per-key throttle applied. CPU on the hosts that were failing stabilized. We still see higher memory churn on a subset of workers, likely related to kv-cache handling in beta-neon-v3.
Miguel C: Good to schedule a full rollback test for beta-neon-v3 on staging and reproduce oom. Will collect minimal repro + logs.
Sofia L: Handoff: I'm going offline in 20m. @Raj P take lead for follow-up and correlation with deploys. Leave page to oncall rotation if needed.
Raj P: On it. I'll validate audit logs, gather stack traces, and coordinate rollback if we need to prevent rollout later.
oncall-bot: Handoff noted. Primary: Raj P, Secondary: Evelyn M.
Priya K: Customer comms: sent interim status at 11:22 UTC, linked monitoring graphs and mitigation steps.
Sofia L: Quick post-mortem checklist: 1) Re-enable beta-neon-v3 only after root cause and regression test 2) Add canary ramp limits for quantized kernels 3) Add per-variant oom alert with host-level tagging 4) Contact customers impacted with summary and timeline
Raj P: I'll own 1 & 4. Miguel will own repro and fix. Evelyn will add alerting and ramp guard. Priya handling customer comms.
Miguel C: Will capture kernel logs and reproduce on a small cluster. ETA 4h for initial root-cause.
Evelyn M: Adding an automated ramp policy now: ```redwoodctl policies create ramp-guard --trigger metric:error_rate --threshold 0.5 --action pause-ramp```
oncall-bot: NOTE: Temporary soft-throttle in effect for expr "qps>20" limiting to 10 qps. Enforced at 11:13 UTC.
Sofia L: Thanks team. If any customer escalates, page me. Otherwise we keep watch and update status in 30m. :thumbsup:
Priya K: Will update support ticket and post a short status update to #general to reduce noisy pings.
Raj P: Leaving a quick artifact link with logs: https://internal.logs/redwood/incident/2123459999 (internal)
Sofia L: Closing the critical page; incident state -> mitigated. We'll move to a P1 writeup if root cause persists.
oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated by traffic demotion and per-key throttles. Incident state: mitigated. Time to mitigated: 12m.
Miguel C: Note to follow: check quant kernel version differences between canary and stable, possible unsafe fallback path.
Evelyn M: I'll schedule a post-incident review tomorrow 10:00 UTC. Invitees: SRE, Runtime, Release Eng, Support.
Sofia L: Thanks all. Closing thread for now.
